sources.title: Cultivating teamwork in esports: a framework for assessment and training
sources.gameScope: Professional Counter-Strike / general esports teamwork applicability
notes: Behavioral trace data from 80 professional gamers across 16 teams
Validated coordination metrics include convergence, view coverage and co-location
Metrics were significantly related to nearly all measured defensive and offensive outcomes
Do not infer an ideal VALORANT spacing distance or that closer co-location is universally better

sources.title: The aiming advantages in experienced first-person shooter gamers: Evidence from eye movement patterns
sources.publisherOrAuthor: Yang et al. / Computers in Human Behavior
notes: 63 participants: 28 experienced FPS players and 35 non-FPS players
Experienced FPS players showed faster execution and more efficient eye-movement patterns
Target distance and appearance latency affected performance
Not a VALORANT-specific experiment

sources.title: Assessment of human expertise and movement kinematics in first-person shooter games
sources.publisherOrAuthor: Donovan et al. / Frontiers in Human Neuroscience
notes: 32 professional or semi-professional FPS players; 4 specialized in VALORANT
Shows a speed-accuracy tradeoff and task-dependent mouse movement kinematics
Statespace Labs/Aim Lab affiliation is a potential conflict-of-interest consideration
Aim Lab task evidence, not direct ranked VALORANT gunfight evidence

sources.title: Impact of focus of attention on aiming performance in the first-person shooter videogame Aim Lab
notes: 37 participants split into higher and lower FPS-experience groups
Found no significant aiming-performance advantage for external focus over internal focus
Useful opposing evidence against overly simple universal mental-focus coaching claims
Not a VALORANT-specific experiment
